column1: # What an HTTP status line means to this repository, read by two suites.
# `xtask/src/store.rs`'s `served` decides whether the log store is up; the
# `Delivery` classifier in `crates/nc-log/src/ship.rs` decides whether a batch of
# log lines was taken. They were written four times between them with different
# answers: only the shipper required the three characters of the code to be
# digits, so `HTTP/1.1 2ab Invented` was a refusal to one and a success to the
#   line          the status line, with `\r` for a carriage return
#   terminator    `crlf` — the reader appends `\r\n\r\n`, an ordinary answer
#                 `none` — the line is the whole answer, nothing follows it
# **Two verdict columns, because the two are not the same question and one of
# the classes they disagree on is real.** `served` asks whether the store said
# 2xx, from a bounded read that may legitimately stop mid-line; the shipper asks
# whether it may discard a batch, and an answer with no terminator is one it
# cannot trust, so it keeps the lines and writes them to stderr. A single
# `2xx`/`not-2xx` column could not carry the unterminated rows at all, and their
# A case added here is answered by both suites or neither run is green, and the
# row count is pinned in both — a floor with room under it let the one row that
# decides the digit clause be deleted along with the clause.
